# [Baseline] - MAC - D - Wifi Corporate

Deploys the corporate network as a Wi-Fi profile to every Mac, so that a device connects automatically after enrolment and a user never needs to know or type the network password.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | macOS |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Device config |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | Own baseline — Intune Wi-Fi profile (macOSWiFiConfiguration), WPA/WPA2-Personal. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.20 and A.8.21, NIS2 art. 21(2)(e). |
| File | [`Baseline_MAC_D_Wifi_Corporate.json`](Baseline_MAC_D_Wifi_Corporate.json) |

> SSID and PSK are set to `<SSID-CORPORATE>` and `<PSK-CORPORATE>`. Fill them in before you assign; with the placeholder in place the profile connects on no device at all. The password ends up in this template and therefore in this repo. There is no CIPP token for a PSK like %OrganizationId% is for the tenant ID, and leaving a placeholder does not work here: Graph never returns a PSK — a tenant backup only includes `preSharedKeyIsSet: true`. So if you fill it in in the tenant instead of here, the next CIPP sync writes the placeholder over it again and every device loses its Wi-Fi. Fill it in here, and only as long as this repo is private; if it is ever shared, rotate the PSK. That the PSK remains a shared secret anyway is already explained in the notes for [Baseline] - WIN - D - Wireless and Peripherals: a local administrator simply reads it with `netsh wlan show profile key=clear`, and the control that does solve that is 802.1X with certificates. Two macOS peculiarities: Apple's Wi-Fi payload has only one personal variant, so `wpaPersonal` covers WPA, WPA2 and WPA3 where Windows has a separate `wpa2Personal`; and macOS has no counterpart of `connectToPreferredNetwork` in this profile type — the preference order there follows from the device's own network order. This is a regular device configuration and not a custom .mobileconfig, so the PSK is a readable field in the template and not hidden in a base64 payload.

## Properties — 7

A classic device configuration has no settingDefinitionIds but fixed properties.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| `ssid` | <SSID-CORPORATE> |
| `networkName` | <SSID-CORPORATE> |
| `wiFiSecurityType` | wpaPersonal |
| `preSharedKey` | <PSK-CORPORATE> |
| `connectAutomatically` | true |
| `connectWhenNetworkNameIsHidden` | false |
| `proxySettings` | none |
